description: Machine-readable form of CONTRACT.md. Every rule here has the same id and the same statement text as the contract prose; test/contract-manifest.test.js asserts both directions, because a checker reporting a rule the contract does not state makes the checker's output a lie.

notes.roles: role is 'widget' or 'host'. The CLI gate (U4) evaluates a widget subject; the in-page inspector (U12) evaluates the host's own proxy surface. A rule whose role does not match the subject is not-evaluable, never a pass.
notes.predicates: Every predicate is { check, params }. 'attestation-claim' reads the widget's attestation and the result carries evidence 'attested'. 'harness-probe' requires an execution harness and is not-evaluable without one. Pattern sets are named, not inlined — src/shared/patterns.js (PRO-9) owns the expressions.
notes.attestationClaims: The claim keys referenced below define the shape of the attestation document a widget supplies under W8: exposedToScoped, untrustedContentMarked, authorizationEnforced, noSensitiveValues.

rules.title: Widget identity is declared, vendor identity is assigned
rules.statement: Declare your widget identifier only; the host assigns the vendor label. A label a widget can assert is one it can forge, capturing or erasing a rival's tool.
rules.note: A registered name of three or more dot-separated segments occupies the vendor segment the host owns. This is a necessary condition, not proof that a widget is not impersonating anyone — the protection against impersonation is H1, where the label comes from the allowlist and the widget's own claim is never read.

rules.title: Exposure is scoped to real embedders
rules.statement: Restrict `exposedTo` to the host origins that actually embed you. A wildcard hands your capability to any page willing to frame you.
rules.note: Not mechanical: the descriptor returned by getTools() carries no exposedTo member (spike Q1). The surface proves only that the caller's own origin was included, never that no wildcard was used.

rules.title: Content you did not author is marked
rules.statement: Mark every tool returning content you did not author with `untrustedContentHint`. Unmarked, another party's text reaches the agent looking like yours.
rules.note: The annotation's value is mechanically readable; whether the returned content is self-authored is not. Only the vendor knows, so only the vendor can attest.

rules.title: Mutating tools declare themselves mutating
rules.statement: Declare `readOnlyHint` truthfully — anything that mutates state, sends a message, or moves money is mutating. A false read-only claim is a side effect nobody was asked to confirm.
rules.note: Not-evaluable without a harness. Ambient claims contradiction detection against instrumented reference widgets whose state changes the harness can see, not generic false-read-only detection for arbitrary widgets.

rules.title: Minimal input, no passthrough
rules.statement: Accept only the parameters the tool needs, never a free-form context or passthrough field, which is an open channel into your execution path.
rules.note: inputSchema arrives from getTools() as a JSON string and must be parsed before evaluation (spike Q1). The name list is a heuristic over unconstrained string properties, not an exhaustive one.

rules.title: Descriptions state capability, not instructions
rules.statement: Describe capability and nothing else; carry no instruction addressed to the agent, because a description is text the model reads, not a caption it ignores.
rules.note: Detection over known shapes. A benign instruction-like description must not fail this rule (R23), and an unrecognized attack shape will pass it.

rules.title: Surface changes are announced
rules.statement: Notify your host when your own tool surface changes, so it does not depend on cross-origin event propagation to learn that it did.

rules.title: An attestation exists and is complete
rules.statement: Supply a machine-readable attestation covering every obligation the registered surface cannot reveal; without one, those obligations are unevaluated rather than passed.
rules.note: Mechanical because presence and shape are verifiable; the claims inside it are not, which is why each attested rule is reported separately as resting on the vendor's word.

rules.title: Authorization is enforced where state changes
rules.statement: Confirm with the user and honor the session's existing permissions before any side effect, because the arrival of a tool call is not authorization.

rules.title: No credentials, secrets, or payment instruments
rules.statement: Neither accept nor return credentials, secrets, tokens, or payment instrument numbers. A secret in a tool result is a secret in the agent's transcript.
rules.note: The accept half is partly screenable through W5's schema check; the return half is not knowable from the surface, so the rule as a whole is attested rather than mechanical. H12 is the host's independent redaction layer over the same shapes.

rules.title: Allowlist admits, and the allowlist names the vendor
rules.statement: Admit tools only from allowlisted origins and take each vendor label from that entry, never from the widget — origin is the one identifier a widget cannot assert.

rules.title: Names are composed, validated, and refused rather than coerced
rules.statement: Name every federated tool `vendor.widget.verb`, and refuse a name that collides, exceeds 128 characters, or carries an illegal character rather than truncating it into one that misattributes its own call.
rules.note: `.` is the separator because tool names permit only ASCII alphanumerics plus `_`, `-`, and `.`, and `.` is the one absent from every official Chrome example.

rules.title: Agent-visible text is rebuilt, never passed through
rules.statement: Rebuild every widget-supplied string an agent will see — descriptions, parameter descriptions, enum values, results — into a host-authored envelope naming the contributing origin; passed through unchanged, vendor text is indistinguishable from yours.

rules.title: Agent-directed instructions quarantine the origin
rules.statement: Detect agent-directed instructions in widget text and quarantine the origin on a match — filtering that lowers exposure, not a guarantee of containment.
rules.note: Evaluated over the host's published surface rather than as a behavioral probe: matched text still present on that surface means the origin was not quarantined. A shape the pattern set does not recognize passes, which is why the limits section calls this filtering rather than containment.

rules.title: Quarantine is per-origin, retroactive, and re-checked every pass
rules.statement: Quarantine by origin and retroactively, withdrawing proxies already registered, and re-evaluate every admitted widget on every pass, because a widget can turn hostile after it loads.

rules.title: The mutating annotation is never weakened
rules.statement: Carry a widget's mutating annotation through unchanged and never present it as read-only, since that annotation is the agent's only cue to ask first.
rules.note: The platform spelling of the plan's untrustedContent is untrustedContentHint; both annotations are carried, and neither is weakened.

rules.title: One instance per identity, refused visibly
rules.statement: Federate one instance per vendor and widget identity and refuse the second visibly, naming the limit — dropped silently it is indistinguishable from a widget that failed to load.

rules.title: Revocation withdraws the grant, not just the proxy
rules.statement: Revoke by withdrawing the origin's `tools` Permissions Policy grant rather than by dropping the proxy alone, which would leave the widget still able to register.

rules.title: The surface stays current and passes do not recurse
rules.statement: Keep the surface current as widgets register and unregister, and serialize overlapping aggregation passes so a pass triggered by your own proxy registrations cannot recurse.
rules.note: toolchange fires for cross-origin children and is correctly scoped, but carries no payload, so re-aggregation is whole-surface and debounced (spike Q4).

rules.title: Failures are envelopes, and late results are discarded
rules.statement: Return a structured failure envelope naming the cause when a proxied tool is unavailable, errors, or exceeds its timeout, and discard a result arriving after timeout or revocation rather than forwarding it.
rules.note: Discarding a late result is not cancellation. The side effect may already have occurred; the inspector reports the race rather than claiming the call was stopped.

rules.title: Bounds are named when breached, never silently applied
rules.statement: Bound what one origin may consume — tool count, metadata size, result size, concurrent executions, change rate — and name the breached bound, because silent truncation makes an over-budget widget look conformant.

rules.title: Sensitive shapes are redacted and logs stay in the session
rules.statement: Redact credential-, token-, and payment-shaped strings before they reach an envelope or a log, and keep logs in memory for the session alone; a log is a second copy of everything that passed through.
rules.note: Redaction alone is verifiable from an envelope, but non-persistence across reloads and non-transmission off the host origin are only visible by running the host, so the rule as a whole is observed.
